sourceIssues.printed: "Lemma 1.1. The group scheme Num_{X/k} is constant if and only if there is an integer d ≥ 0 with the following property: For every invertible sheaf L on X̄ there is a numerically trivial invertible sheaf N on X̄ such that L^{⊗d} ⊗ N is the pullback of some invertible sheaf on X."
sourceIssues.reason: With d = 0 the property holds trivially (take N = O), so the "if" direction would fail: P¹_C, viewed as a proper R-scheme, has X̄ = P¹_C ⊔ P¹_C with Num = Z² and complex conjugation exchanging the two factors, so Num_{X/R} is not constant. Noted by the extraction (item 2).

review.reason: Confirmed, with the reach corrected from 'nothing' to 'a stated result' by this review. The statement is verbatim in arXiv:2004.07025v3, the version the errata names: I re-fetched the PDF on 23 September 2026 and its SHA-256 is ae6481f25627867473ba40db3b08e5f4b861de8aa103204eefc5ad1123a46d61, matching the recorded hash, and read the LaTeX e-print (sha256 ae77260256b42df57443f3101ccda9bf2bbbc2f991410bf27f02b0e0afdc87d9) at every locator: 'there is an integer $d\geq 0$'. Since the condition is existential in d and d = 0 makes it hold for every X — take N = O, which is numerically trivial and is the pullback of O_X — the lemma as printed asserts that Num_{X/k} is always constant. The recorded counterexample settles that it is not: for X = P¹_C regarded as a proper R-scheme, X̄ = P¹_C ⊔ P¹_C, Num = Z² and complex conjugation exchanges the factors. So the lemma itself is false as printed, which is a stated result, not nothing; the entry's own reason already says the 'if' direction fails. Nothing downstream uses the false reading — the sufficiency argument in the proof ('the Galois action becomes trivial on some subgroup of finite index') needs d ≥ 1 — so the main theorem is untouched, and the correction 'an integer d ≥ 1' stands.

review.reason: Confirmed, and the counterexample checks out. The statement is verbatim in arXiv:2004.07025v3, the version the errata names: I re-fetched the PDF on 23 September 2026 and its SHA-256 is ae6481f25627867473ba40db3b08e5f4b861de8aa103204eefc5ad1123a46d61, matching the recorded hash, and read the LaTeX e-print (sha256 ae77260256b42df57443f3101ccda9bf2bbbc2f991410bf27f02b0e0afdc87d9) at every locator. The printed proof of (ii)⇒(iii) says 'The curve C ⊗ Ω is birational to P¹_Ω, because Γ(S_ā) → Γ(S_a) is a graph isomorphism', and a graph isomorphism carries no information about a single smooth fibre, where it holds trivially. sourceIssues.printed: "Each triple (L, a, b) where L is an invertible R-module and a ∈ L, b ∈ L^{⊗−1} are elements with a ⊗ b = 2R yields a finite flat group scheme G^L_{a,b}, characterized by G^L_{a,b}(A) = {f ∈ L ⊗_R A | f^{⊗2} = a ⊗ f}, with group law f_1 ⋆ f_2 = f_1 + f_2 + b ⊗ f_1 ⊗ f_2."

review.reason: Confirmed. The group law is verbatim in arXiv:2004.07025v3, the version the errata names: I re-fetched the PDF on 23 September 2026 and its SHA-256 is ae6481f25627867473ba40db3b08e5f4b861de8aa103204eefc5ad1123a46d61, matching the recorded hash, and read the LaTeX e-print (sha256 ae77260256b42df57443f3101ccda9bf2bbbc2f991410bf27f02b0e0afdc87d9) at every locator as 'f_1\star f_2=f_1+f_2+ b\otimes f_1\otimes f_2'. Both checks in the entry are right. With L = R = Z, a = 1 and b = 2 the scheme is {f : f² = f} = {0,1}, the constant group the text names next, and the printed law sends (1,1) to 4, which is not in it, while the minus sign sends it to 0. With a = 2 and b = 1 the scheme is {0,2}, identified with μ₂ by f ↦ 1 − f, and (1−f₁)(1−f₂) = 1 − (f₁+f₂−f₁f₂) is the minus sign again. The minus sign is also the Oort–Tate convention.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Proposition 5.5, p.16, in arXiv 2004.07025v3 (9 August 2022, SHA-256 ae6481f2…6d61), whose text after the first page agrees with the author's third revised version of 19 July 2022 (the journal's revision date); the typeset Annals text (197 (2023), 1–63) was not obtained
sourceIssues.printed: "One the other hand, using Hensel's Lemma, any F_2^alg-valued point for Y → S can be extended to an A-valued point. Again with Proposition 5.4 we conclude that a family of canonical covering X ⊗ A → Y ⊗ A exists, whence X_F has good reduction over A, contradiction." (Here X_F is the generic fiber of the canonical covering constructed over Z[1/2], and A = W(F_2^sep), F = Frac A.)
sourceIssues.correction: Compare the two covers: over F they are canonical covers of the same Enriques surface and may differ by a twist by a class in H¹(F, μ₂) = F^×/F^{×2}. One way to close the gap: construct the local cover over Z₂ (using a Z₂-point, which exists since #Y(F₂) = 25 by Corollary 7.3), write the difference over Q₂ as (−1)^e 2^a 5^b, remove (−1)^e 2^a by twisting the Z[1/2]-cover by the étale torsor s² = (−1)^e 2^a, and 5^b by twisting the local cover by the unramified torsor Z₂[z]/(z² − z − 1); then both covers agree over Q₂ and give a smooth proper model everywhere, contradicting Fontaine.
sourceIssues.reason: Canonical coverings are unique only up to such twists, so good reduction of the local cover over A does not by itself give good reduction of X_F. The extraction supplies the four-twist repair sketched in the correction (report, "Four-twist repair"). The main theorem is not in doubt.

review.reason: Confirmed. The passage is verbatim in arXiv:2004.07025v3, the version the errata names: I re-fetched the PDF on 23 September 2026 and its SHA-256 is ae6481f25627867473ba40db3b08e5f4b861de8aa103204eefc5ad1123a46d61, matching the recorded hash, and read the LaTeX e-print (sha256 ae77260256b42df57443f3101ccda9bf2bbbc2f991410bf27f02b0e0afdc87d9) at every locator. The gap is real: for an Enriques surface Y over a field F of characteristic ≠ 2, the canonical cover is Spec(O_Y ⊕ ω_Y) with an algebra structure that depends on a trivialisation of ω_Y^{⊗2}, unique only up to Γ(Y, O_Y)^× = F^×, and rescaling it by λ twists the cover by the class of λ in H¹(F, μ₂) = F^×/(F^×)². So the cover built over A and the base change to F of the cover built over Z[1/2] agree only up to such a twist, and good reduction is not invariant under one. The entry's four-twist repair is a sensible way to close it, and the main theorem is not in doubt. (The same sentence also opens 'One the other hand', an orthographic slip that carries no mathematics; it is visible in the quotation and is not recorded separately.)

Tsen's theorem gives Br(F) = 0 for a function field of a curve over an algebraically closed field; here F = F₂(t). The cyclic algebra (F₄(t)/F₂(t), t) is nonzero: the extension is constant, hence unramified with residue degree 2 at t = 0, so every norm has even valuation there and t is not a norm. The proposed repair — pass to F₂^alg(t), where Tsen applies, and take Galois invariants — is the standard route.
